verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is NASA's crew exploration vehicle for the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: NASA’s Orion spacecraft is carrying humanity to the Moon... on Artemis missions (R2); The Orion Multi-Purpose Crew Vehicle (MPCV) is a partially reusable crewed spacecraft used by NASA for the Artemis lunar exploration program (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Orion is NASA's spacecraft for Artemis program.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is designed to carry four astronauts on deep-space missions including lunar orbit and future Mars missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Orion is the first spacecraft built for astronauts destined for deep space (R1); Four astronauts will venture around the Moon in Orion on Artemis II (R2); Orion supports a crew of four beyond low Earth orbit (R6); Designed to carry humans to the Moon, Mars and beyond (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm design for 4 crew on deep space including lunar and Mars missions.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is 67 feet tall.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: full stack height 67 ft
verifications.reasoning: R13 directly states Orion full stack height as 67 ft.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is a three-part capsule consisting of launch abort, crew, and service modules.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Orion spacecraft is made of three primary elements - the launch abort system, the crew module, and the service module (R12)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to three-part description.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is built to handle deep space radiation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: protecting astronauts from radiation (R1); Radiation Protection: Needed to protect crew... from cosmic and solar radiation seen in deep space (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention radiation protection for deep space.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is built to handle high-speed atmospheric re-entry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: how the spacecraft endures its high speed return from deep space... heat shield (R1); Orion’s heat shield during re-entry (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Direct references to heat shield for high-speed re-entry.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the first crewed mission under the agency’s Artemis campaign (R2); first to fly a crew aboard Orion (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II as first crewed Orion flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch the first crew on a lunar flyby in April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: lifted off... at 6:35 p.m. EDT (R3, dated 2026/04/01); launch astronauts to the moon on April 1 (R5); April 1, 2026 (Artemis II) (R6); LaunchED April 1, 2026 (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm April 2026 launch for crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is designed for four crew members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Four astronauts will venture around the Moon in Orion (R2); Crew capacity 4 (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent across sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft can hold more crew members in emergency situations.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention capacity for more crew in emergencies.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft offers more space than Apollo.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Orion’s crew module provides 57 percent more habitable volume of space than the Apollo capsule
verifications.reasoning: Direct comparison confirms more space.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is capable of operating for up to 21 days with crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: up to 21 days undocked (R6); up to 21 days (R11); Up to 21 days (R13)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match across sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is capable of operating for six months docked at the Lunar Gateway.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: up to six months when docked (R6); six months in orbit when docked to the Gateway (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft comprises the Crew Module, the European Service Module, and the Launch Abort System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: crew module (CM), ... European Service Module (ESM) ... Launch Abort System (LAS) (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Standard composition listed.

verifications.claim: The Crew Module provides living space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: where crew will live and work on their journey
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated.

verifications.claim: The European Service Module provides power, propulsion, water, and air.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: supplying it with the electricity, propulsion, thermal control, air and water (R12); propulsion, thermal control, and electrical power... life support systems including water, oxygen, and nitrogen (R13)
verifications.reasoning: Matches listed functions.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft features a heat shield for 25,000 mph re-entry speeds.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: re-enters... at speeds nearing 24,000 mph (R9); 24,600 mph... 24,700 mph (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Sources cite ~24,000-24,700 mph; 25,000 is close but not exact.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft's launch abort system can pull the crew to safety in milliseconds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: It can activate within milliseconds to pull the vehicle to safety
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft utilizes solar array wings on the service module for power.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: solar array wings (SAWs) have fully deployed... on the European Service Module (R3); four solar array wings to provide power (R12)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described.

verifications.claim: Artemis I completed an uncrewed test flight in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: uncrewed Orion capsule launched on Artemis 1 in November 2022 (R5); Artemis I November 16, 2022 (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Confirmed date and uncrewed status.

verifications.claim: Artemis I proved the Orion spacecraft’s systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: to certify the spacecraft's flight systems in lunar orbit
verifications.reasoning: Directly states certification/proof of systems in deep space.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first time humans return to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: carrying humans beyond the Moon for the first time in more than 50 years (R4); NASA's first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources use similar phrasing for crewed lunar mission after 50+ years.

verifications.claim: As of 2026, multiple Orion capsules are under construction or completed for subsequent missions including Artemis III and IV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: As of 2026, three flight-worthy vehicles had been built... Three additional flight-worthy vehicles are under construction
verifications.reasoning: Confirms multiple built/under construction for future missions.
